SAPS CAR THEFT RACKET

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Deals on wheels - SAPS and vehicle theft syndicates working together?

Unique Selling Point:
Imagine having your car stolen, only to get an offer from a policeman who says he can facilitate you buying it back from the syndicate who stole it from you...Certain scams around the recovery of stolen motor vehicles are rife in SA. Particularly one where the victim gets a call from a supposed SAPS member who says he has recovered their vehicle, and is asking for money for a tow truck to tow it back to a SAPS lot. But in the case of Mmbara Mashudu, who's vehicle was stolen in Midrand at the beginning of this year, it's a whole different ball game. Mashudu was told that a policeman from Silverton Police station could help him recover his vehicle, if he paid the syndicate who had stolen it from him R20 000...

Summary:
Mashudu agreed to the offer. On the day he was to get his vehicle back he recorded all his conversations with the policeman on his phone's voice recorder. He has provided us with the recording and the evidence is damning. He also took some video footage of the police car and police men who accompanied him, which he has also provided to us. After paying R20 000, the police accompanied him to the Mamelodi cemetery where his car had been left by the syndicate. He claims the police are working with the syndicates.

Further information:
We also have a case study for the scam - Erika da Cruz. After her car was stolen, she was warned by the SAPS member at the police station that she might get a call from someone claiming to be saps and needing money to tow the car. She did get a call, the very next day. The man wanted R3500 for towing. She told him she had heard this was a scam. The following two days the scammers get phoning her. She refused. We have traced one of the cell phone numbers back to a man who was employed by SAPS, but left in 2010. The question, one only the police can answer, is is the phone a SAPS phone and someone else now has it or is it the ex-members phone? Either way a scary thought and more evidence of police involvement. Have asked her if she would be willing to do a sting but her husband is adamant that they not get involved like that as they fear reprisals. She is however happy to tell her story on camera.

Richard Brussouw from the NHPA says scam problem is rife - he estimates that up to 40% of people who have their cars stolen get the phone calls. He has put a lot out about it on social media etc. Says the info either comes from SAPS leaks, Eatis system etc etc.

Extra Budget Items:
WG agreed that we could fly Mashudu down from Cape Town, where he lives. He has asked if he can rather drive. He said he would need R3000. It seems in line with or even cheaper than a return flight. Can we approve R3000 for his travel?

Script:


SAPS Vehicle Theft Racket
10 November 2020
First Draft


Voice
46 921 vehicles were stolen in South Africa last year, an average of 128 cars every day. Victims rely on the South African Police Service to bring the perpetrators to book, but who do you turn to when the police themselves are allegedly involved with the vehicle theft syndicates?

Link Derek
The statistics speak for themselves, it’s an unfortunate reality of life in South Africa. But now we get a case where the police say they can get your stolen vehicle back, but first they have to buy it back from the syndicate.

Voice
In December last year Mashudu Mmbara’s Audi A5 was stolen during a house robbery at his brother’s house in Midrand, Johannesburg.

Sound Up Mashudu
Derek: It was stolen from this house in Midrand, what exactly happened?

Mashudu: The guys broke into the house, they stole a TV, and I assume they put everything in the car and then they drove away.

Voice
Mmbara reported the case at the Midrand Police station, and also posted pictures of the missing vehicle on social media.

Sound Up Mashudu
I had put this on Facebook, on social medias. Lots of people gave calls, gave me a call to say we will assist.

Voice
But one call in particular, from a man Mmbara had never met before, sounded promising.

Sound Up Mashudu
Whom he said look I’ve got contacts within the police services, I’ve got this police officer by the name of Raymond Lekwatsima, he will be able to find out something. Give him a call. But surely he will want something in return, just to assist you. He said he knows lots of these guys that steal the vehicles within the Pretoria vicinity.

Voice
After phoning Lekwatsima, Mmbara arranged to meet with him at Pretoria Central police station two days after his vehicle was stolen. He took these images of Lekwatsima on his cell phone on the day in question. Lekwatsima arrived in full police uniform, accompanied by two other police officers, driving this police vehicle.

Sound Up Mahudu
There were three cops in that K9 Golf GTI.

Voice
Mmbara alleges Lekwatsima told him that he could buy his vehicle back from the syndicate for R20 000 in cash.

Sound Up Mmbara
And that they will recover the vehicle, all I needed was just to give them money to recover the vehicle.

Voice
He managed to make this voice recording of officer Lekwatsima talking about how the deal would work on his cell phone.

Sound Up Voice Recording of Lekwatsima (46m22s)
Lekwatsima: We have to give that money to somebody else then they give us the surety that the car you'll get it. I give you the surety that the car you will find it. You just have to stick around and you must not go anywhere until we get the guy who will go to the guys give them the money and then they will leave it where we can find it.

Voice
Desperate to get his car back, which wasn’t insured at the time, Mmbara drew the cash and accompanied by the policemen left for Mamelodi in the East of Pretoria.

Sound Up Mashudu
Then he jumped in the back of my car, we drove to Pretoria East.

Voice
Mmbara, managed to secretly film this footage along the way. While they were driving, he says Lekwatsima asked to see the cash.

Sound Up Mashudu

I gave him the R20 000 in cash. And then he counted it. And he then made contact with his guy on the other side to say the money is there.

Voice
The police stopped in Nellmapius, a suburb next to Mamelodi. Mmbara says he was told that the money would be handed over to the syndicate in this street.

Sound Up Mashudu
Eventually a tow truck came from that direction.

Voice
Mmbara was allegedly told that the tow truck was there to collect the money on behalf of the syndicate.

Sound Up Mashudu
Then he took the money and handed over to the tow truck. And then the tow truck drove off.

Link Derek
With the money counted and handed over to the mysterious tow truck driver, Mmbara then spent several hours with the police waiting for his car to be released by the syndicate. The cops even dragged him to other crime scenes in the area.

Sound Up Mashudu
It was traumatising in that I’m not a trained police officer, I should not be involved in crime scenes, and put my life in danger.

Voice
Lekwatsima apparently received a call and was told the vehicle could be found here, at Mamelodi West Cemetery. The police escorted Mmbara to the sight and they found his car - just two days after it had been stolen.

Sound Up Mashudu
Derek: Quite a strange place to be reunited with your car at the West Cemetery in Mamelodi?

Mashudu: Ja Derek you are quite right it’s a very strange place to be, but this is right here where the vehicle was parked. And I must tell you coming in I was having a sigh of relief that again I have been reunited with my vehicle.

Voice
Lekwatsima allegedly told Mmbara to keep mum about the payment to the syndicate, and that the case would be handled as a normal vehicle recovery.

Sound Up Mashudu
The officer Mr Lekwatsima said look just be happy that we got your vehicle, but we’re not going to go chase… Don’t worry about who brought it here and so on and so forth.

Voice
Mmbara, who says he played along with the police simply to get his vehicle back, laid corruption charges at the Midrand Police station in January this year - but to date he hasn’t had any feedback from the police.

Sound Up Mmbara
It is very painful for a victim to be paying a police officer to do their job.

Voice
Raymond Lekwatsima declined our offer to be interviewed, so we spoke to provincial police spokesperson Brigadier Mathapelo Peters

Sound Up Brig Peters
Derek: What can you tell us about this case when it’s alleged that police members facilitated the buying back of a stolen vehicle from a syndicate?

Brig Peters: So once I was contacted by Carte Blanche we obviously went on a full on investigation… so our anti-corruption unit is busy with that investigation currently so we’ll see what the outcome is.

Derek: But almost a year later Brigadier, why has it been delayed for so long?

Brig Peters: That forms part of the investigation, we don’t know how far this would go, we don’t know what happened because what was also confusing was while we were trying to do our own quick research was that one minute we were told that the case is at Midrand, the one time it was at Silverton, but eventually we traced it to Pretoria Central.

Voice
So while the case was bounced around between police stations, nothing much came of it until our request for an interview.


Sound Up Brig Peters
DereK: Now it’s alleged that some of the police members were from the Silverton K9 unit?

Brig Peters: That’s what the allegations are saying and like I said we were able to establish that indeed there was a Silverton K9 unit vehicle on the spot of the crime scene.

Derek: It’s alleged that one of the main roleplayers from Silverton was a man named Raymond Lekwatsima, is he still a member of the police?

Brig Peters: This investigation by the Anti-Corruption Unit has basically only started last week. So we will follow the necessary steps in terms of disciplinary procedures as well.

Derek: Is he still a member of the police, has he been suspended?

Brig Peters: For now I want to take a guess that yes, the person could still be in the employ of the SAPS.

Voice
Brigadier Peters says that we’ll have to wait for the outcome of the Anti-Corruption Unit investigation before they’ll be able to answer all our questions, and has this warning for members of the public.

Sound Up Brig Peters
Because this person should not have paid, so whether wittingly or unwittingly, they were also part of the corruption.

Voice
And because of that it’s quite difficult to establish whether this is an isolated incident or part of a much larger issue.

Link Derek
The problem is many other victims don’t come forward to tell their stories. But several viewers have complained to us about a completely different scam - but also involving motor vehicle theft.

Voice
Erika da Cruz from Johannesburg’s bakkie was stolen in October this year. She reported the incident at the Edenvale Police Station. The policeman on duty explained that should they recover her vehicle, it would be impounded and they would contact her - there would never be a fee involved.

Sound Up Erika
He told me that if I was contacted outside of this process, I need to be aware that this is a scam.

Voice
The scam is a simple yet effective one. Criminals phone victims of motor vehicle theft, pretending to be police. They’ll ask for a fee, usually about R3000, to supposedly have the victims car towed to a secure police storage facility. Da Cruz says she got a call from the scammers the day after she reported her car as stolen.

Sound Up Erika
and he had indicated that he had found the vehicle in Komatipoort. They had arrested three suspects. He was very uncomfortable leaving the vehicle at the border. And this went on for about ten minutes, quite thorough, he had my case number, he knew what car I had, he had my name, my surname. He indicated that the tow truck driver was there to be be to put the vehicle on a flatbed, I would have to pay the tow-truck driver R3200 to get the vehicle to Johannesburg.

Voice
Since she’d been warned about the scam, da Cruz told the man she knew it was all a lie and hung up. But many people aren’t that lucky says Richard Brussouw, an ex policeman who has nearly 30 years experience in motor vehicle theft .

Sound Up Richard
Derek it happens quite often, if there are 10 cars stolen or hi-jacked in South Africa, I would say three out of ten you will get the phone call claiming that the vehicle has been recovered.



Voice
Brussouw says the scammers are able to get your details through E-Natis - government’s National Traffic Information System
.

Sound Up Brussouw
They then phone a contact, the robbers now, either working police, traffic, licence department, that goes on the ENATIS system and he gets all the details.

Voice
Brigadier Peters says they aware of the scam.

Sound Up Brig Peters
But what I want to emphasise Derek is that police will never phone you to say that we’ve recovered your vehicle you need to pay, for me that is key.

Voice
The last few weeks have seen many high ranking police officials arrested on charges of corruption in a variety of cases, and Peters says they are determined to restore public confidence in the service.

Sound Up Brig Peters
Well it’s not anything to feel good about, but what is comforting is that when we do find these corrupt elements within our system, within our ranks, they are dealt with decisively. They are not spared any mercy.






SAPS CAR THEFT RACKET Promos

Promo 1
Imagine having your car stolen, but instead of police arresting the criminals, they say you need to buy it back from them. We investigate allegations of police involvement in vehicle theft syndicates.

Promo 2
We investigate claims that some police in Pretoria are in bed with car thieves, after they assisted a man to buy back his stolen vehicle from the very syndicate that stole it in the first place.

Promo 3
A new twist on police corruption as we expose law enforcement officials who helped a man buy back his car from a vehicle theft syndicate - instead of arresting the perpetrators.

Sound Up Erika He told me that if I was contacted outside of this process, I need to be aware that this is a scam. Voice The scam is a simple yet effective one. Criminals phone victims of motor vehicle theft, pretending to be police. They’ll ask for a fee, usually about R3000, to supposedly have the victims car towed to a secure police storage facility. Da Cruz says she got a call from the scammers the day after she reported her car as stolen. Sound Up Erika and he had indicated that he had found the vehicle in Komatipoort. They had arrested three suspects. He was very uncomfortable leaving the vehicle at the border. And this went on for about ten minutes, quite thorough, he had my case number, he knew what car I had, he had my name, my surname. He indicated that the tow truck driver was there to be be to put the vehicle on a flatbed, I would have to pay the tow-truck driver R3200 to get the vehicle to Johannesburg. Voice Since she’d been warned about the scam, da Cruz told the man she knew it was all a lie and hung up. But many people aren’t that lucky says Richard Brussouw, an ex policeman who has nearly 30 years experience in motor vehicle theft . Sound Up Richard Derek it happens quite often, if there are 10 cars stolen or hi-jacked in South Africa, I would say three out of ten you will get the phone call claiming that the vehicle has been recovered. Voice Brussouw says the scammers are able to get your details through E-Natis - government’s National Traffic Information System . Sound Up Brussouw They then phone a contact, the robbers now, either working police, traffic, licence department, that goes on the ENATIS system and he gets all the details. Voice Brigadier Peters says they aware of the scam. Sound Up Brig Peters But what I want to emphasise Derek is that police will never phone you to say that we’ve recovered your vehicle you need to pay, for me that is key. Voice The last few weeks have seen many high ranking police officials arrested on charges of corruption in a variety of cases, and Peters says they are determined to restore public confidence in the service. Sound Up Brig Peters Well it’s not anything to feel good about, but what is comforting is that when we do find these corrupt elements within our system, within our ranks, they are dealt with decisively. They are not spared any mercy. SAPS CAR THEFT RACKET Promos Promo 1 Imagine having your car stolen, but instead of police arresting the criminals, they say you need to buy it back from them. We investigate allegations of police involvement in vehicle theft syndicates. Promo 2 We investigate claims that some police in Pretoria are in bed with car thieves, after they assisted a man to buy back his stolen vehicle from the very syndicate that stole it in the first place. Promo 3 A new twist on police corruption as we expose law enforcement officials who helped a man buy back his car from a vehicle theft syndicate - instead of arresting the perpetrators.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Deals on wheels - SAPS and vehicle theft syndicates working together?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Imagine having your car stolen, only to get an offer from a policeman who says he can facilitate you buying it back from the syndicate who stole it from you...Certain scams around the recovery of stolen motor vehicles are rife in SA. Particularly one where the victim gets a call from a supposed SAPS member who says he has recovered their vehicle, and is asking for money for a tow truck to tow it back to a SAPS lot. But in the case of Mmbara Mashudu, who's vehicle was stolen in Midrand at the beginning of this year, it's a whole different ball game. Mashudu was told that a policeman from Silverton Police station could help him recover his vehicle, if he paid the syndicate who had stolen it from him R20 000...
metadata.Summary: Mashudu agreed to the offer. On the day he was to get his vehicle back he recorded all his conversations with the policeman on his phone's voice recorder. He has provided us with the recording and the evidence is damning. He also took some video footage of the police car and police men who accompanied him, which he has also provided to us. After paying R20 000, the police accompanied him to the Mamelodi cemetery where his car had been left by the syndicate. He claims the police are working with the syndicates.
metadata.Further information: We also have a case study for the scam - Erika da Cruz. After her car was stolen, she was warned by the SAPS member at the police station that she might get a call from someone claiming to be saps and needing money to tow the car. She did get a call, the very next day. The man wanted R3500 for towing. She told him she had heard this was a scam. The following two days the scammers get phoning her. She refused. We have traced one of the cell phone numbers back to a man who was employed by SAPS, but left in 2010. The question, one only the police can answer, is is the phone a SAPS phone and someone else now has it or is it the ex-members phone? Either way a scary thought and more evidence of police involvement. Have asked her if she would be willing to do a sting but her husband is adamant that they not get involved like that as they fear reprisals. She is however happy to tell her story on camera. Richard Brussouw from the NHPA says scam problem is rife - he estimates that up to 40% of people who have their cars stolen get the phone calls. He has put a lot out about it on social media etc. Says the info either comes from SAPS leaks, Eatis system etc etc.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: WG agreed that we could fly Mashudu down from Cape Town, where he lives. He has asked if he can rather drive. He said he would need R3000. It seems in line with or even cheaper than a return flight. Can we approve R3000 for his travel?
